There is no LIS. Laboratory work today is a CPOE order with one free-text result, plus a separate store for interfaced results. Nothing joins the two. Re-verified against the code on 3 October 2026; the highest migration is still 47 (server/migrations.py:5446-5494, _m47_vitals_carried_from at :5417).

ORDERS (the only lab ordering path)
- Table: orders, with type and status CHECKs (server/database.py:805-822). order_events references orders(id) (database.py:826), so orders is an FK parent. Widening its CHECK would be the FK-parent rebuild trap (migrations.py:4697-4720).
- orders_service is the only writer of orders.status: INSERT at orders_service.py:141, UPDATE at :194 (transition) and :252 (result). order_sets_service.py:1063 only sets order_set_application_id.
- State machine (orders_service.py:32-39): draft to active/cancelled; active to in_progress/resulted/cancelled; in_progress to completed/resulted/cancelled; completed, resulted and cancelled are terminal. completed to resulted is illegal.
- Orders are created as draft or active (orders_service.py:77-151). Activation is either create_order(status='active') or transition draft to active.
- TWO manual paths change a lab order: POST /orders/{id}/transition takes any to_status under ORDER_WRITE (orders_routes.py:478-491), and POST /orders/{id}/result (orders_routes.py:494). Nurses hold ORDER_WRITE (permissions.py:124-125).

- Result: one free-text result_text per order, written once in an IMMEDIATE transaction since F072; a different second text gets 409 (orders_service.py:206-257).
- Billing turns lab, imaging and procedure orders in status completed OR resulted into charge candidates by orders.code (billing_service.py:183-187, 797-829). A manually 'completed' lab order therefore bills.

TERMINOLOGY
- 33 LOINC codes, display text only (terminology_service.py:60-94). No units, panels, specimens or ranges. scripts/load_terminology.py does not exist (W103).

OBSERVATIONS (structured results)

The chart lab card (vigil_routes.py:105-148) and the downtime pack (downtime_service.py:268-292) therefore order by julianday(COALESCE(observed_at, recorded_at)) DESC, id DESC. 1. PRINCIPLES
- LIS state lives in new lab_ tables keyed on orders.id. orders.status and order_type CHECKs are never widened (orders is an FK parent).
- An order with lab_order_items is LIS-managed for life, whatever ORB_LAB says. Only lab_order_service changes its status, through conn-taking orders_service helpers.
- Released values go ONLY into observations, one row per analyte, so the chart card, ward pack, timeline and Tier 1 pick them up through the shared reader with no new lane.
- No lab_result clinical_documents copy (buildLabTrends merges both stores, so a copy double-plots).
- No FOREIGN KEY in any lab_ table and no REAL columns. Values are value_milli INTEGER plus decimal_places 0..3 per test.
- Flags and limits are compared at reporting precision (half-up), mirroring the NEWS2 charted-value ruling.
- Not configured is not zero. Orb ships no reference ranges and no critical limits (LIS-R1, LIS-R2). With no approved range the report says "Reference range not configured" and carries no H/L flag. H/L come only from an approved range; HH/LL only from an approved critical limit.
- Time: stored instants use clinical_time.utc_iso_now() / to_utc_iso(). observed_at is the specimen collection instant. Hospital-day logic uses hospital_time.local_day_bounds_utc (midnight local). Every read of observations orders and compares by julianday(COALESCE(observed_at, recorded_at)), then id DESC, because interfaced rows keep their received spelling. Lab tables written only by LIS code store one canonical spelling and order by (timestamp DESC, id DESC).
- All DB work runs in def handlers or run_db.
- No autoverification. A human technically validates and a signatory authorises every result.
- Bedside tests (ward_poct) never enter the LIS.
- Every switch defaults to the strictest behaviour until its ruling lands.

2. FEATURE FLAGS AND MODULE STATE
- config.py gains _module_opt_in(env): True only for 1/true/yes/on; blank or unset is OFF. (Whichever HIS epic lands first adds it; the rest reuse it.)
- ORB_LAB (LAB_ENABLED) is the module switch. HOSPITAL_MODULE_ENV['lab'] = 'ORB_LAB'.
- Sub-switches, all opt-in and all OFF by default:
  - ORB_LAB_ANALYSER_LISTENER (needs ORB_LAB): starts the MLLP listener. ORB_LAB_MLLP_PORT default 2576 (2575 is the monitor feed).
  - ORB_LAB_CRITICAL_SWEEP_S: sweep period, default 60.
  - ORB_RESULT_QUARANTINE: unresolved INGESTION results go to the queue instead of NULL-patient rows. The analyser lane always uses the queue.
  - ORB_RESULT_CORRECTIONS: an external OBX 'C' supersedes the prior final.
  - ORB_ORU_ORDER_LINK: external ORU results link to and close CPOE lab orders (lis-21).
  - ORB_LAB_CRITICAL_INTERFACED: an external OBX-8 HH/LL/AA raises a lab critical callback (lis-22). Works without ORB_LAB.
  - ORB_LAB_PORTAL_REPORTS: portal shows LIS reports (lis-29).
- services/lab_module.py holds the module state, computed at startup with run_db and refreshed by the lab sweep loop, cached in memory so /api/health never touches the DB:
  - 'on': ORB_LAB set.
  - 'draining': ORB_LAB unset but open lab work exists (lab_order_items not in released/cancelled, lab_results entered or tech_validated, or an open lab_critical_notifications row). Intake stops; lab roles keep the Lab tab to finish, cancel or release work; the ward critical card, acknowledgement, lab-mediated cancel and the sweep keep running; compliance_service reports a failing check "Laboratory module switched off with open work: N specimens, M critical results".
  - 'off': nothing open. Every /api/lab route returns 404 {error: module_disabled, module: 'lab'}.
  - Critical surfaces (card, acknowledge, sweep) also run when ORB_LAB_CRITICAL_INTERFACED is on.
- /api/health: modules.lab = state != 'off'; module_states.lab carries the string. No counts, no PHI.
- Cutover: lab_module_events (append-only). At startup with ORB_LAB on and no 'enabled' since the last 'disabled', insert 'enabled' at now; with ORB_LAB off after an 'enabled', insert 'disabled'. intake and ensure_intake consider only orders whose activation instant (order_events new_status 'active', or created_at when created active) is at or after the latest 'enabled'. Months of historical 'active' lab orders never flood the collection lists, and orders activated while the module was off stay on the free-text path for life.
- routes/lab_routes.py: router dependency require_lab_module(allow_draining) read at request time (dietary_routes.py:118 pattern).
- Frontend: HospitalModuleId gains 'lab'; OPT_IN_MODULE_IDS = ['lab'] with DEFAULT_MODULE_FLAGS.lab = false, so the cache fails toward HIDDEN for opt-in modules; DIAGNOSTIC_MODULE_IDS = ['lab'] and MONEY_MODULE_IDS = hospital modules minus CLINICAL minus DIAGNOSTIC. Panel ./pages/panels/LabPanel.tsx.
- With every switch off: no tab, /api/lab 404, CPOE lab orders and /orders/{id}/result behave exactly as today, no cards, lab tables stay empty, terminology unchanged, Ward Record and demos untouched. The one ungated change is lis-5's reader parity fix (see risks).

3. ROLES AND PERMISSIONS (roles.py stays the single authority)
- STORABLE_ROLES gains lab_technician, pathologist (any authorised signatory: pathologist, biochemist, microbiologist) and phlebotomist, via one users rebuild through _rebuild_users_role_check, merged with other HIS epics' roles where they land together.
- Lab roles are hospital-wide (no department), not in DEPARTMENT_REQUIRED_ROLES, and hold no patient.read_all, relay.* or sage.query. Every lab-surface read is audited.
- New permissions: lab.read, lab.collect, lab.receive, lab.result, lab.authorise, lab.master, lab.critical_log, lab.critical_ack, lab.interface, and ingest.reconcile (attach or discard an unmatched result).
- Grants:

| Role | Permissions |
|---|---|
| phlebotomist | lab.read, lab.collect |
| lab_technician | lab.read, collect, receive, result, critical_log, ingest.reconcile |
| pathologist | the technician set, plus lab.authorise and lab.master |
| nurse | lab.collect, lab.critical_ack |
| doctor | lab.collect, lab.critical_ack |
| admin | lab.read, lab.interface, ingest.monitor (list only) |

- ingest.reconcile is never granted to a department-scoped role in v1 (a parity test enforces it), because the queue shows raw identifiers hospital-wide (LIS-R17).
- Mirrored in src/lib/roles.ts. ROLE_CONFIG: lab roles get home 'lab' and tabs ['lab']; when modules.lab is false they get a ModuleOffNotice home ("The laboratory module is switched off on this site. Ask your administrator."), never an empty shell. 'lab' is not in CLINICAL_MODULE_IDS; doctors and nurses reach lab work through Orders, the nurse Samples view and the critical card.
- Scope: ward-facing endpoints use department_scope plus scope_patient_ids_sql (404, never 403). Lab-facing endpoints are hospital-wide and call log_phi_read.

ACCESSION NUMBER (LIS-R13)
- 12 numeric digits: YYMMDD of the hospital-local day (midnight rollover via local_day_bounds_utc), a 5-digit daily sequence, and a Damm check digit (detects every single-digit error and every adjacent transposition, including 09/90). Optional site prefix.

5. ORDER LIFECYCLE (the guard)
- orders_service.transition_order and add_result check EXISTS lab_order_items for the order. If present they raise OrderManagedByLab, mapped to 409 by orders_routes: "This order is managed by the laboratory. Results arrive from the laboratory; cancel it from the laboratory request." Draft to active is unaffected (items appear only after activation). Keyed on the items, never on ORB_LAB.
- New conn-taking helpers in orders_service (transition_in_conn, set_lab_result_text_in_conn) keep the legality check and order_events row but skip the guard; only lab_order_service calls them.
- Lab-mediated cancel: POST /api/lab/orders/{order_id}/cancel (ORDER_WRITE with patient scope, or lab.receive; reason required; served in 'draining'). It cancels every item not yet released, withdraws their entered or tech-validated results ("Order cancelled"), cancels specimens left with no live items, and reconciles the order. The worklist shows "Cancelled by <name> at <time>" so the bench stops.
- reconcile_order_status(conn, order_id): all items cancelled gives cancelled (never billed); at least one released and the rest released or cancelled gives resulted, with result_text "Reported in the laboratory system. Open the laboratory report for values." (fixed text, no accession or version, so amendments never make it stale); otherwise in_progress once any specimen is collected, else active. A rejected item blocks completion until recollected or cancelled and appears on the lab's "Rejected, no decision" list and the ward Samples view.
- Release never depends on order state. If reconcile finds an unexpected terminal state (a pre-guard manual completion), the release still commits, a lab_exceptions 'order_state_conflict' row is written in the same transaction, and logger.error fires.
- OrdersPanel: the list response gains lab_managed and an item status summary; for lab-managed orders the next-status and + Result buttons are hidden and Cancel calls the lab cancel with a reason.
- Billing: unchanged code. Resulted orders bill by orders.code; all-cancelled orders become cancelled and do not bill; a partially cancelled panel bills the panel code (see risks).

11. DISCHARGE, TRANSFER AND LATE RESULTS

- Late results after discharge (blood cultures) release normally into observations and reports.
- Routing of post-discharge criticals is new ruling LIS-R19. Whether discharge should warn about an open lab critical belongs to held R009 and is not built. Until LIS-R19 is ruled the lab closes by phone callback (LIS-R3 closure i).

product_rulings.question: LIS-R1: Does Orb ship any default critical limits, and who approves the site's critical value list?
product_rulings.options: (a) ship none; the pathologist enters each limit and names the clinicians it was agreed with, and a test with no approved limit raises no critical; (b) ship suggested limits inactive until approved; (c) ship active defaults
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), with a printable worksheet of common critical analytes and blank limits. W083 and W108 already call this NABH policy.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R2: Does Orb ship default reference ranges?
product_rulings.options: (a) none: 'Reference range not configured' and no H/L flag; (b) suggested ranges inactive until approved; (c) active textbook defaults
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Ranges depend on analyser, method and population.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R3: Critical callback policy: who is called, how fast, and what closes a callback?
product_rulings.options: Tiers in site.toml. Closure by (i) the lab's phone log with recipient name and read-back; (ii) in-app acknowledgement by a clinician on the patient's ward with read-back; (iii) the Relay post itself
product_rulings.recommendation: Tier 1 ward nurse in charge plus the ordering doctor via the case room, 15 minutes; Tier 2 attending or duty doctor, 15 minutes; Tier 3 duty medical officer. The site checks timings against its NABH policy. Close by (i) or (ii), never (iii). An undelivered post (no case room) counts as tier due at once.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R4: When is a critical value communicated, and is the unauthorised value visible?
product_rulings.options: (a) at technical validation, marked 'Preliminary, not yet authorised' in the Relay post and card, chart shows released only; (b) only after authorisation; (c) at entry
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). NABL practice; waiting for a visiting pathologist delays a potassium of 7.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R5: May one person enter, technically validate and authorise the same result?
product_rulings.options: (a) a technician can never authorise; a signatory may do all steps, recorded and counted; (b) a site setting requires two different people; (c) always two people
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), with (b) available. Until ruled, the setting ships ON (two people), the strictest default.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R6: Patient identification and timing at collection, with no wristband barcodes yet
product_rulings.options: Labels printed in advance or at the point of collection; how far back collected_at may be set
product_rulings.recommendation: Confirm name and UHID on screen before labels print and print at the point of collection; batch pre-printing only at the lab's own counter; back-dating up to 2 hours with a reason. Until ruled, back-dating is refused.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R7: Which range applies when date of birth or sex is not recorded?
product_rulings.options: (a) no range, no flag, and the report says why; (b) adult 'any' range; (c) refuse to release
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Only ranges covering every age (or sex 'any') still apply. Critical limits still apply when the approved limit does not depend on age or sex. patients.age is never used because it is static.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R8: Autoverification of analyser results
product_rulings.options: (a) none in v1; (b) rules-based release of normal results
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Every result gets human technical validation and authorisation, which also keeps the LIS clear of IVD-software arguments while R023 is held.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R9: Delta checks: what a flag does, and who sets thresholds
product_rulings.options: (a) technologist reason before technical validation; (b) hard block; (c) display only
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Thresholds per analyte by the lab director; none ship active; comparator values are never delta-checked.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R10: Who is told when a released result is amended or withdrawn?
product_rulings.options: (a) a case-room notice for every amendment, plus the critical flow when it crosses a critical limit or range boundary; (b) notice only for flag changes; (c) silent version change
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), plus a NABH incident prompt when a wrong-patient result is withdrawn.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R11: Should patients see LIS lab reports in the portal?
product_rulings.options: (a) off; (b) authorised reports immediately; (c) after a site delay or a clinician's release
product_rulings.recommendation: Off by default; (c) when a site turns it on; flags as printed text with no colour, matching the portal vitals ruling.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R12: Which new staff roles, and how much do lab roles reach?
product_rulings.options: lab_technician, pathologist and phlebotomist; or reuse admin accounts
product_rulings.recommendation: The three roles; 'pathologist' covers any authorised signatory; hospital-wide, with no Relay, Sage or patient.read_all; nurses and doctors can also collect.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R13: Accession number format
product_rulings.options: Numeric or alphanumeric; length; check digit; day rollover; overflow
product_rulings.recommendation: 12 digits: YYMMDD of the hospital-local day (rollover at local midnight), a 5-digit sequence, then a Damm check digit (catches every single-digit error and adjacent transposition, unlike plain mod-10 or Luhn on 09/90). Numeric only for older analysers and Code 128C. Refuse loudly at 99999, never wrap. Optional site prefix.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R14: How far does the analyser layer go?
product_rulings.options: (a) framework plus HL7 adapter now, ASTM when a site supplies protocol documents, per-analyser profile at onboarding; (b) vendor drivers in the product
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). A hospital's existing middleware is accepted as an HL7 source; each analyser takes 1 to 3 field days with the vendor's document.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R15: Label and scanner hardware
product_rulings.options: Browser printing to thermal printers, or a ZPL print server
product_rulings.recommendation: Browser printing to 50 x 25 mm thermal printers at each ward station and the lab, USB keyboard-mode scanners, procured by the hospital; no print server in v1.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R16: When does an order show 'resulted', and are partial panels visible?
product_rulings.options: (a) resulted when at least one item is released and every other item is released or cancelled, each analyte visible as authorised; all-cancelled orders become cancelled; (b) nothing visible until the whole panel is released
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), with pending analytes shown as pending on the report and rejected items blocking completion until recollected or cancelled.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R17: Who may attach an unmatched result to a patient, or discard it?
product_rulings.options: (a) lab roles only (hospital-wide, already see raw identifiers); (b) lab roles plus doctors (raw identifiers from other wards become visible to a ward doctor); (c) a new medical-records role; (d) admin
product_rulings.recommendation: (a) now, (c) later; never (d), because attaching is a wrong-patient decision that feeds Tier 1, the chart and the ward pack. A site without lab staff keeps ORB_RESULT_QUARANTINE off.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R18: Which tests are done at the bedside and stay outside the LIS?
product_rulings.options: Starter catalogue marks capillary ketones, VBG and ABG as ward_poct; the lab director can reclassify; or put every lab code through the LIS
product_rulings.recommendation: Ship those three as ward_poct, because the DKA and asthma order sets repeat them hourly at the bedside; the lab director reclassifies per site (for example ABG run in the lab). Reclassification applies to orders activated afterwards.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R19: Who receives a lab critical for a patient who has been discharged or is mid-transfer? (Sits beside held R009 and does not decide it.)
product_rulings.options: (a) the lab phones the discharging consultant and logs it; (b) the last ward's card plus the case room; (c) both
product_rulings.recommendation: (c) until a site policy says otherwise; notifications are never auto-closed by discharge or transfer. Whether discharge should warn about an open lab critical is part of R009 and is left to that ruling.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R20: Do the lab critical surfaces (the Laboratory Relay post and the ward CriticalLabCard) fall inside held R023's intended-use scope?
product_rulings.options: (a) no: they relay the lab's own flag against a pathologist-approved limit, with no Orb-computed severity or score, like a phone call; (b) yes: hold them with the Vigil chip (lis-17)
product_rulings.recommendation: Samuel decides. The design presents them as lab communication (option a) and builds them behind ORB_LAB, but marks go-live as blocked on this ruling so R023 is not decided by implication. lis-17 (Vigil board chip) stays build-blocked on R023.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R21: What happens to LIS work when ORB_LAB is switched off?
product_rulings.options: (a) drain: intake stops, lab roles finish open work, ward critical card and sweep keep running, compliance report shows a failing check until empty; (b) hard off: everything disappears; (c) refuse to switch off while work is open
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Hard off hides open criticals and half-processed specimens.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R22: Should Orb raise a critical callback from an external lab's OBX-8 HH/LL/AA flag (the W083 follow-up)?
product_rulings.options: (a) yes when a site turns ORB_LAB_CRITICAL_INTERFACED on, using the same tiers and read-back acknowledgement; (b) display only; (c) never
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), off by default; Orb relays the sending lab's own flag and never computes one; the external lab's own phone call is logged as the ward's read-back acknowledgement.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R23: Should lab critical delivery be part of the pilot's shadow evidence?
product_rulings.options: (a) not in v1: evidence lives in lab_critical_events and the TAT dashboard; (b) add a 'lab' shadow lane, which needs an out-of-transaction rebuild of the self-referencing shadow_events table
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). The pilot's headline metric is NEWS2-based; revisit with a planned shadow schema change.

risks: Honest size: about 92 engineer-days for everything (about 18 weeks), against roadmap B10's 4 to 5 weeks. The cut line (lis-1 to lis-16, lis-18, lis-19, lis-23 to lis-25: manual LIS, criticals, TAT, quarantine and HL7 intake through existing middleware) is about 72 days. The smallest shippable manual LIS (lis-1 to lis-11, lis-14, lis-15) is about 47.5 days. Deferred: ASTM (7 days), simulator, portal, external order linkage and interfaced criticals until their inputs or rulings arrive.

Building this contradicts the approved Ward Record sales plan. Every switch is opt-in and the client cache defaults the lab tab to hidden; today the cache fails toward visible for all modules (shellConfig.tsx:236-253).

lis-5 is the one ungated change: Tier 1's creatinine lane gains the void, simulated and julianday tie-break rules the chart and ward pack already apply, on every profile. That is a parity defect fix (a voided creatinine can raise a Tier 1 flag today). If Samuel wants zero default-profile change it can sit behind ORB_LAB, at the cost of keeping that defect.

julianday() orders mixed spellings correctly but cannot fix naive interfaced times, which it reads as UTC; a device sending naive IST is 5.5 hours off in delta checks and latest-result picks until that feed sets an assumed timezone.

Interfaced rows keep labTrends' 1.5x/0.7x range heuristic for 'critical', so the chart can still call an interfaced creatinine of 2.0 critical. Only LIS rows use the lab's flag. Changing interfaced behaviour is a separate clinical question.

FK-parent trap: orders.status and order_type CHECKs are never widened; the guard and lab tables carry LIS state. Users roles are a rebuild that commits the runner's open transaction (migrations.py:4697), so HIS epics should share one roles rebuild.

Hardware is a hospital purchase: thermal label printers, keyboard-mode scanners, serial-to-TCP converters. v1 identification is two identifiers confirmed on screen.
A visiting pathologist cannot sign out remotely from a LAN-only appliance; remote access is a hospital IT decision, and LIS-R5's two-person default blocks a one-pathologist lab until ruled.

issues.issue: The design closes only the free-text /orders/{id}/result path (lis-6). It leaves /orders/{id}/transition and the OrdersPanel next-status button open. Any ORDER_WRITE holder, nurses included, can move an LIS-managed order to in_progress, completed, resulted or cancelled behind the lab's back. 'completed' is terminal and completed->resulted is illegal. lis-10's release then hits an order the conn-taking helper cannot result: either the whole IMMEDIATE release rolls back (a validated critical potassium can never reach the chart) or the release lands on an order the CPOE shows as done. The order also bills early, because billing counts 'completed' and 'resulted' alike. A clinician can also cancel an order after the specimen is received or analytes are released, and the design only defines 'cancel before receipt'.
issues.evidence: orders_routes.py:478-491 (transition takes any to_status under ORDER_WRITE). orders_service.py:32-39 (active->resulted and in_progress->completed are legal; completed is terminal). OrdersPanel.tsx:90-97 (nextStatus offers 'completed' for in_progress) and :454-458. billing_service.py:797-829 (_COMPLETED_ORDER_STATUSES covers completed/resulted). The design's 409 sits only in orders_routes.add_result.
issues.fix: Put the guard in orders_service, not the route. An order that has lab_order_items, whatever ORB_LAB says, refuses manual in_progress, completed and resulted transitions with 409 'managed by the laboratory'. Cancellation after receipt goes through a lab-mediated cancel that cancels unreleased items and leaves released ones. OrdersPanel hides the next-status button for LIS-managed orders. Add tests: a nurse POSTs /transition completed on an LIS order and gets 409; cancel after receipt is refused or lab-mediated; release on an order that cannot be resulted fails loudly in a test, not silently.

issues.issue: The design assumes the chart lab card needs no change ('it already reads observations and shows SimulatedBadge'). That is false. buildLabTrends never passes source for observation rows, so the card shows LIS-simulated results (lis-23) with no Simulated label, which breaks the honesty-label rule. Separately, labStatus derives 'critical' from the range (more than 1.5x high or less than 0.7x low) and ignores the laboratory's flag whenever a range parses. A potassium of 7.0 against 3.5-5.1 that the lab phones as an approved-limit critical (HH) shows only 'high'. A creatinine of 2.0 against 0.7-1.3, which has no approved critical limit, shows 'critical'. The same screen then carries two conflicting meanings of critical.
issues.evidence: src/lib/labTrends.ts:196-201 (observation add() omits the simulated arg, default false at :173); :150-164 (range heuristic wins, flag consulted only when there is no range). VigilPanel.tsx:1821 (badge keyed on lab.simulated).

Write abnormal_flag HH/LL into observations only from approved critical limits. Add a vitest for each case.

issues.issue: lab_observations.previous_result and the Tier 1 tie-break order and compare by raw observed_at strings. observations.observed_at is stored as received, with 'T' or a space, offset or naive, because migration 43 canonicalised only vitals and risk_scores. issues.issue: lis-18 (external ORU linked to orders) has four problems. (a) It is not flag-gated, yet it changes order status and therefore billing on the default (Ward Record) profile. (b) It can only match if the external LIS carries Orb's orders.id (uuid4) in OBR-2. Outbound ORM/OML is out of scope, and W108 says placer handling needs a real LIS message sample first, so in practice it never matches. (c) It sets order_id on a placer match without requiring the order's patient to equal the resolved PID patient, which risks wrong-patient linkage. (d) 'Resulted when every ordered code has a final row' is undefined for panels, because orders.code is the panel code (58410-2) and OBX rows carry component codes.

HOSPITAL_FUNCTION_COVERAGE row 'Outbound orders (ORM/OML)' is Absent. billing_service.py:827-829.

Define completion by OBR-4 (universal service id) against orders.code, not by OBX codes. Mark it blocked on a real site ORU sample, or pair it with an outbound-order increment. Until then, keep only the 'OBX C supersedes prior final' half, which needs no placer match.

issues.issue: Quarantine attach (lis-17) is gated on ingest.monitor for the ingestion lane, and only admin holds that permission. Admin has no department, so department_scope returns None and the 'scope check' passes for every patient. A non-clinical governance account would decide which patient a lab result belongs to. That is a wrong-patient decision, and the attached result immediately feeds Tier 1, the chart and the downtime pack. The lane is also not flag-gated, so the sold Ward Record product changes.

A new ingest.reconcile permission, held by a clinical or lab role (doctor, nurse, lab_technician), covers attach, with a two-identifier confirmation (name plus UHID against the raw PID) and the reason in fail-closed clinical_access audit. Add a product ruling on who may reconcile identity, and test that admin attach returns 403.

issues.issue: The lab critical Relay lane ignores the existing clinical-alert lane and repeats its known failures. (1) It posts via raw relay_service.send_message with no message:new push, so a case room already open never shows the critical until reopened (fixed for nurse alerts on 2026-10-03). (2) It has no 'patient has no case room' branch. (3) The sender is the technologist, a role with no relay.read, who can never see the ward's reply. (4) It emits no shadow event, though shadow is the pilot's evidence instrument. issues.issue: Turning ORB_LAB on or off is unsafe in both directions. On: if ensure_intake sweeps active lab orders without items, every historical lab order left 'active' (nothing results them today, per W152) floods the collection lists with months-old specimens. Off: open critical notifications, in-flight specimens and entered but unreleased results vanish. The tab, /api/lab and the home cards all disappear, and the free-text 409 is keyed on ORB_LAB, so nurses can free-text-result half-processed LIS orders.

issues.fix: Record a lab_cutover_at instant, and have intake and ensure_intake consider only orders activated after it. Key the 409 and transition guard on lab_order_items existence, not on the flag. While ORB_LAB is off and open criticals or unreleased items exist, keep the critical card and the sweep running, or surface the condition loudly on the ops and Trust Center page. Test both transitions.

issues.issue: The order-completion rule is wrong at the edges. The principle 'resulted = every item released or cancelled' makes an order whose items were all cancelled 'resulted', and billing then charges for a test that was never performed. A rejected item with no recollection leaves the order in_progress forever. result_text 'Laboratory report <accession> v<n>' is written once (F072), so it goes stale after a lis-12 amendment, and it is ambiguous when one order spans several accessions.
issues.evidence: Design sections 1 and 5. billing_service.py:797-829 bills resulted or completed orders. orders_service.py:200-255 (result written once).
issues.fix: An order is resulted when at least one item is released and the rest are released or cancelled. When all items are cancelled, the order is cancelled. Rejected items need an explicit recollect or cancel, and an overdue list shows the ones with neither. result_text names no version or accession ('Laboratory report: see LIS'), and the report link carries both. Add tests for an all-cancelled order (no bill) and a rejected item with no recollection.

issues.issue: Five smaller hazards: (1) intake merges new items into an existing planned specimen even after its label was printed, so the tube's label lists the wrong tests. There is no LIS. Laboratory work today is a CPOE order with one free-text result, plus a separate store for interfaced results. Nothing joins the two. Verified against the code on 3 October 2026 (highest migration is 47, server/migrations.py:5494).

ORDERS (the only lab ordering path)
- Table: orders, with type and status CHECKs (server/database.py:805-822). order_events references orders(id) (database.py:826), so orders is an FK parent. Widening its CHECK would be the FK-parent rebuild trap (migrations.py:4697-4720).
- State machine draft > active > in_progress > resulted/cancelled (orders_service.py:32-40).
- create_order only checks that the code exists in the named terminology system (orders_service.py:114-127). The form offers LOINC, SNOMED and ICD10 for every order type (OrdersPanel.tsx:65), so an ICD-10 code can order a lab.
- Order sets create lab drafts with LOINC or local codes (order_sets_service.py:1025; site_config/order_sets.json lab items: lactate, CBC, BMP, ORB-LAB-BLOOD-CULTURE).
- Result: one free-text result_text per order. Since F072 it is written once, in an IMMEDIATE transaction; a different second text gets 409 "chart a correction as a clinical note" (orders_service.py:206-257).
- Any ORDER_WRITE holder can result, and nurses hold ORDER_WRITE (orders_routes.py:494; permissions.py:124-125). Orders are ward-scoped and audited on read (orders_routes.py:403-448).
- Nothing is sent outward: there is no ORM, OML or ASTM code anywhere.

TERMINOLOGY
- 33 LOINC codes, display text only (terminology_service.py:60-94). No units, panels, specimens or ranges.
- scripts/load_terminology.py does not exist (W103).

OBSERVATIONS (structured results)
- Table (database.py:398-419): source, observation_code, value_numeric REAL, reference_range text, abnormal_flag, free status, observed_at, panel_name, obr_group_id. There is no order link.
- Writers: ingestion_service._insert_observation (ingestion_service.py:1183-1255) and history import (source history_import).
- An unresolved patient is inserted with patient_id NULL and a log warning (ingestion_service.py:1194-1206) (W109).
- The HL7 adapter stores OBR-2, the placer number, as obr_group_id (ingestion_adapters.py:338) but never matches it to an order. A corrected OBX ('C') is stored beside the original.
- Readers: chart lab card (vigil_routes.py:121-148, with a void-status filter, newest first), downtime ward pack (downtime_service.py:57, 270-292), Tier 1 creatinine (patient_specific_screen.py:534-575), timeline (patient_timeline_service.py:464-475), admin counts (admin_routes.py:251).

first_draft.design:
Ordered: principles, feature flag, roles, data model, services, routes, UI, audit, links to the other epics.

1. PRINCIPLES
- LIS state lives in new lab_ tables keyed on orders.id. orders.status and order_type CHECKs are never widened (orders is an FK parent).
- LIS states map onto the existing order vocabulary: active = ordered, in_progress = first specimen collected, resulted = every item released or cancelled, cancelled.
- Released values go ONLY into observations, one row per analyte. The chart lab card, ward pack, timeline and Tier 1 then pick them up with no new lane.
- No lab_result clinical_documents copy. buildLabTrends merges documents and observations, so a copy would double-plot every point.
- No FOREIGN KEY in any lab_ table (migration 20/23/25 rule). Every lab table is a leaf, so a later CHECK change is an ordinary in-transaction rebuild.
- No REAL columns. A value is value_milli INTEGER plus decimal_places 0 to 3 per test. Limits are *_milli.
- Flags and limits are compared at reporting precision (half-up), mirroring the NEWS2 charted-value ruling. observations.value_numeric = value_milli/1000 at release; value_text is rendered at decimal_places (keeps trailing zeros).
- Not configured is not zero. Orb ships NO reference ranges and NO critical limits (rulings LIS-R1, LIS-R2). With no approved range a value prints "Reference range not configured" and carries no H/L flag.
- Time:
  - Stored instants use clinical_time.utc_iso_now() / to_utc_iso().
  - observed_at = the specimen collection instant.
  - Hospital-day logic (accession sequence, TAT buckets) uses hospital_time.local_day_bounds_utc.
  - Previous/latest result reads ORDER BY observed_at DESC, id DESC.
- All DB work runs in def handlers or run_db (sync SQLite on the loop is the known wedge).
- No autoverification. A human technically validates and a signatory authorises every result.

2. FEATURE FLAG
- config.py: new _module_opt_in(env) beside _module_enabled. It is True only for 1/true/yes/on; blank stays OFF.
- LAB_ENABLED = _module_opt_in("ORB_LAB"). HOSPITAL_MODULE_ENV["lab"] = "ORB_LAB". enabled_modules()["lab"] is published on /api/health.
- Sub-switches:
  - ORB_LAB_ANALYSER_LISTENER: opt-in, needs ORB_LAB.
  - ORB_LAB_MLLP_PORT: default 2576 (2575 belongs to the monitor feed).
  - ORB_LAB_CRITICAL_SWEEP_S: default 60.
- routes/lab_routes.py carries a router-level require_lab_module() that returns 404 {error: module_disabled, module: lab}. It is read at request time (dietary_routes.py:118 pattern).
- Frontend:
  - HospitalModuleId gains 'lab'.
  - New OPT_IN_MODULE_IDS. DEFAULT_MODULE_FLAGS.lab = false, so the cache fails toward HIDDEN for opt-in modules. Today it fails toward visible (shellConfig.tsx:249).
  - Panel path ./pages/panels/LabPanel.tsx.
- With ORB_LAB off:
  - no tab, and /api/lab/* returns 404;
  - CPOE lab orders and the free-text /orders/{id}/result path behave exactly as today;
  - no lab cards on the nurse or doctor home;
  - the migrations still run, and their tables stay empty.
- The Ward Record profile and the demos are untouched.

3. ROLES AND PERMISSIONS (roles.py stays the single authority)
- STORABLE_ROLES gains lab_technician, pathologist and phlebotomist. pathologist means any authorised signatory: pathologist, biochemist or microbiologist.
- This is one users-rebuild migration via _rebuild_users_role_check, ideally merged with every other HIS epic's new roles into a single rebuild.
- Lab roles have no department (hospital-wide, like the pharmacist) and are NOT in DEPARTMENT_REQUIRED_ROLES.
- Lab roles hold no patient.read_all, relay.* or sage.query. They see patients only through lab surfaces, and every read is audited.
- New permissions in permissions.py:
  - lab.read: worklists, specimens, reports.
  - lab.collect: print labels and mark collected.
  - lab.receive: receipt, rejection, recollection.
  - lab.result: entry, technical validation, delta acknowledgement.
  - lab.authorise: clinical validation, amend, withdraw.
  - lab.master: tests, panels, ranges, critical limits, analyser test-code maps.
  - lab.critical_log: the lab records a callback.
  - lab.critical_ack: the ward acknowledges with read-back.
  - lab.interface: analyser connection settings.
- Grants:

| Role | Permissions |
|---|---|
| phlebotomist | read, collect |
| lab_technician | read, collect, receive, result, critical_log |
| pathologist | the technician set, plus authorise and master |
| nurse | collect, critical_ack |
| doctor | collect, critical_ack |
| admin | read, interface |

- Mirrored in src/lib/roles.ts.
- ROLE_CONFIG: the three lab roles get home 'lab' and tabs ['lab']. Admin gets 'lab' through HOSPITAL_MODULE_TABS.
- 'lab' is NOT added to CLINICAL_MODULE_IDS. Doctors and nurses reach lab work through Orders, the nurse Samples view and the critical card.
- Scope: ward-facing endpoints use department_scope plus scope_patient_ids_sql (404, never 403). Lab-facing endpoints are hospital-wide and call log_phi_read.

4. DATA MODEL
Migration numbers are assigned at merge (other work in progress also adds migrations). All changes are additive, with no FKs.

M-A lab_contract (lis-3): the contract the later increments add rows and routes to, the migration 20 precedent.
- lab_sections: id TEXT PK ('BIOCHEM', 'HAEM', 'CLINPATH', 'SEROLOGY', 'MICRO'), name, site_id NULL, active, sort_order.
- lab_specimen_types: code PK, display, container, container_colour_name, min_volume_ul INT, stability_minutes INT NULL, handling_note, active.
- lab_tests:
  - Identity: id TEXT PK, code, code_system CHECK ('LOINC', 'LOCAL'), name, short_name (16 chars or fewer, for labels), kind CHECK ('analyte', 'panel').
  - Bench and specimen: section_id, specimen_type_code.
  - Result shape: result_type CHECK ('numeric', 'text', 'coded'), unit, decimal_places CHECK 0..3, coded_values_json, orderable.
  - TAT targets: tat_routine_min, tat_urgent_min, tat_stat_min. NULL means no target.
  - Delta check: delta_kind CHECK ('absolute', 'percent') NULL, delta_threshold_milli, delta_window_hours.
  - is_send_out (reserved), active, version, updated_by, updated_at.
  - UNIQUE(code_system, code).
- lab_panel_components: panel_test_id, component_test_id, sort_order. PK (panel_test_id, component_test_id).
- lab_reference_ranges:
  - Columns: id, test_id, sex CHECK ('any', 'male', 'female'), age_min_days, age_max_days, low_milli NULL, high_milli NULL, display_text, effective_from, effective_to NULL, approved_by, approved_at, method_note.
  - Values are never UPDATEd. A change closes effective_to and inserts a new row.
- lab_critical_limits: same shape, with critical_low_milli, critical_high_milli and agreed_with.
- lab_rejection_reasons: code PK (haemolysed, clotted, insufficient, unlabelled, mislabelled, wrong_container, delayed, leaked, other), display, incident_prompt, active.
- lab_accession_counters: hospital_day PK, last_seq. Incremented under BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
- lab_specimens:
  - Identity: id TEXT PK, the accession number.
  - What: patient_id, specimen_type_code, container, priority.
  - status CHECK ('planned', 'collected', 'received', 'rejected', 'in_process', 'completed', 'cancelled').
  - Labels: planned_at, label_printed_at, label_print_count.
  - Collection: collected_at, collected_by, collection_location, identity_check_json.
  - Receipt: received_at, received_by, receipt_note.
  - Rejection: rejected_at, rejected_by, rejection_code, rejection_note, recollect_of.
  - site_id, created_at, updated_at.
  - Indexes: (status, priority, received_at), (patient_id, created_at).
- lab_specimen_events: append-only. specimen_id, seq, event_type, actor_user_id, actor_role, occurred_at, detail, metadata_json. UNIQUE(specimen_id, seq).
- lab_order_items:
  - Columns: id INT PK, order_id, patient_id, test_id, panel_test_id, specimen_id NULL, section_id, priority, cancelled_reason, created_at, updated_at.
  - status CHECK ('awaiting_collection', 'collected', 'received', 'resulted', 'tech_validated', 'released', 'cancelled', 'rejected').
  - UNIQUE(order_id, test_id).
- lab_results:
  - Identity: id INT PK, order_item_id, order_id, specimen_id, patient_id, test_id, version.
  - Value: value_milli NULL, comparator CHECK ('<', '>', '<=', '>=') NULL, value_text, unit, decimal_places, comment.
  - Judgement: reference_range_id, reference_range_text (a snapshot), abnormal_flag CHECK ('', 'L', 'H', 'LL', 'HH', 'A'), critical_limit_id, is_critical.
  - Delta: delta_flag, delta_json, delta_ack_by, delta_ack_at, delta_ack_reason.
  - Entry: entry_method CHECK ('manual', 'analyser'), instrument_id, ingestion_event_id, entered_by, entered_at.
  - Sign-off: tech_validated_by, tech_validated_at, released_by, released_at.
  - status CHECK ('entered', 'tech_validated', 'released', 'superseded', 'withdrawn'), amend_reason, superseded_by_result_id.
  - Links: observation_id, source CHECK ('lis_manual', 'lis_analyser', 'simulated').
  - Partial UNIQUE(order_item_id) WHERE status NOT IN ('superseded', 'withdrawn').
- lab_result_events: append-only, with before_json and after_json.
- lab_critical_notifications:
  - Columns: id TEXT PK, result_id, patient_id, test_id, value_display, preliminary, raised_at, raised_by, current_tier, tier_due_at.
  - raised_in_department is a display snapshot only, never a scope.
  - Callback: relay_message_id, acknowledged_at, acknowledged_by, recipient_name, recipient_role, method CHECK ('phone', 'in_person', 'in_app'), read_back.
  - Closure: closed_at, closed_by, close_reason, policy_json.
  - status CHECK ('open', 'acknowledged', 'closed_unreachable'). Partial UNIQUE(result_id) WHERE status = 'open'.
- lab_critical_events: append-only, same shape as escalation_events.

M-B observations_lab_links (lis-5):
- observations ADD COLUMN order_id TEXT, specimen_id TEXT, lab_result_id INTEGER, superseded_by INTEGER.
- Indexes: (order_id), (lab_result_id), (patient_id, observation_code, observed_at).
- ADD COLUMN only; nothing references observations.

M-C result_quarantine (lis-17):
- Columns: id, payload_json, reason, created_at.
  - lane CHECK ('ingestion', 'analyser').
  - What arrived: ingestion_event_id, raw_patient_identifier, raw_specimen_id, instrument_id.
  - status CHECK ('open', 'attached', 'discarded').
  - Resolution: attached_patient_id, attached_observation_id, attached_result_id, resolved_by, resolved_at, resolution_reason.
- Plus a one-time idempotent sweep that copies NULL-patient observation rows into the queue.

M-D lab_analysers (lis-19):
- lab_instruments:
  - Columns: id PK, name, make, model, serial, section_id, host, port, assumed_timezone, biomedical_asset_id, enabled, last_message_at.
  - protocol CHECK ('hl7v2', 'astm').
  - transport CHECK ('http', 'mllp_listen', 'tcp_client', 'tcp_listen').
- lab_instrument_test_map: instrument_id, instrument_code, test_id, factor_milli DEFAULT 1000, active, approved_by, approved_at. PK (instrument_id, instrument_code).

ACCESSION NUMBER
- 11 numeric digits: YYMMDD (hospital day) + a 4-digit sequence + a mod-10 check digit. Optional site prefix.
- Assigned when the specimen is planned. The check digit is validated on every scan or typed entry.

5. SERVICES (flat services/, like the rest)
- lab_observations.py: the one live-result reader.
  - VOID_OBSERVATION_STATUSES (adds 'superseded'), live_observations_sql(alias), previous_result(db, patient_id, code, before).
  - Adopted by vigil_routes.py:121-148, downtime_service.py, patient_specific_screen.py (which also gains the void, simulated and id DESC rules) and patient_timeline_service.py.
  - A guard test fails on any new FROM observations in services/ or routes/ that bypasses it.
- lab_master_service.py:
  - Catalogue search; test and panel CRUD with versioning; range and limit approval; applicable_range(test, sex, age_days).
  - Registers every orderable code in terminology (LOCAL displays end "(site lab code)"), so orders_service validation passes.
  - Loads site_config/lab_catalogue.starter.json: tests, panels, specimen types, sections and rejection reasons, with no ranges and no limits.
- lab_accession.py: the counter and the check digit.
- lab_order_service.py:
  - intake(order_id): idempotent. It explodes panels and plans specimens grouped by specimen type, container and priority. Items merge into an existing planned specimen for the same patient.
  - Called post-commit from orders_service on activation, with ensure_intake() as a sweep backstop.
  - Unmapped codes go to an exceptions list.
  - Also: cancel propagation, collection lists, collect (moves the order active to in_progress through orders_service), receive, reject, recollect.
- lab_result_service.py:
  - Entry, edit before validation, flags, delta, technical validation.
  - authorise_and_release runs in ONE IMMEDIATE transaction:
    - lab_results set to released;
    - an observations INSERT with order_id, specimen_id, lab_result_id, source and status 'final' (or 'corrected');
    - the order set to resulted when complete, with result_text "Laboratory report <accession> v<n>", through new conn-taking orders_service helpers;
    - an order_events row;
    - the audit row.
  - amend and withdraw supersede the old observation: status 'superseded' plus superseded_by.
- lab_report_service.py: the report payload.
- lab_critical_service.py:
  - Raises a critical at the ruled point (LIS-R4).
  - Posts to Relay post-commit via relay_service.send_message (relay_service.py:837) into the patient's case room:
    - idempotency_key "lab-critical:<id>";
    - sender = the technologist, never bot_lab (migration 46 treats bot_lab rows as simulated).
  - A failed post leaves the notification open.
  - Callback log, in-app acknowledgement, and sweep_loop() started in the main.py lifespan beside the escalation sweep.
  - Tiers come from site.toml [lab.critical] and [[lab.critical.tiers]], validated by site_config_service like [escalation].
- lab_tat_service.py: per-specimen intervals (ordered, collected, received, released); aggregates by section, priority and hospital day.
- result_quarantine_service.py: list, attach (scope check, one transaction, audit), discard (reason). ingestion_service._insert_observation sends unresolved events there instead of NULL-patient rows.
- services/lab_analyser/:
  - framework.py: the AnalyserAdapter ABC (identify, parse to list[AnalyserResult], ack) plus a shared conformance test suite.
  - router.py: maps instrument codes to tests and writes 'entered' results with entry_method 'analyser' and source lis_analyser. Unknown specimens or codes go to quarantine. An ingestion_events provenance row is written with source_type 'lab_analyser'.
  - hl7_adapter.py: reuses hl7v2.parse and build_ack. The specimen id comes from SPM-2, OBR-3 or OBR-2.
  - listener.py: reuses MllpFramer with the same finish-the-batch contract, on its own port.
  - astm_framer.py: E1381 ENQ/ACK/NAK/EOT, frame numbers, ETB/ETX, checksum. Bounded and exception-free.
  - astm_records.py: E1394 H, P, O, R, C, Q and L records, with delimiters read from H.
  - astm_adapter.py, astm_transport.py.
  - host_query.py: answers a Q record with the ordered tests for an accession.
  - simulator.py: DEMO_MODE only, source 'simulated'.

6. ROUTES (/api/lab, all behind require_lab_module)
- Catalogue and master:
  - GET /catalogue?q= (order.read or lab.read).
  - /master/tests, /master/panels, /master/ranges, /master/critical-limits, /master/specimen-types, /master/rejection-reasons: lab.read for GET, lab.master for writes.
- Specimens:
  - GET /collection (lab.collect; ward-scoped for department accounts).
  - GET /collection/labels.
  - POST /specimens/{id}/collect.
  - GET /specimens/scan/{code}.
  - POST /specimens/{id}/receive, /reject and /recollect (lab.receive).
  - GET /specimens/{id}.
- Results:
  - GET /worklists/{section_id}.
  - POST /results and PATCH /results/{id} (lab.result).
  - POST /results/{id}/delta-ack and /results/tech-validate (lab.result).
  - POST /results/authorise (lab.authorise, batch per specimen).
  - POST /results/{id}/amend and /withdraw (lab.authorise, reason required).
- Reports:
  - GET /reports/{accession} (lab.read).
  - GET /reports/patient/{patient_id} (lab.read, or require_patient_access(ORDER_READ) for ward clinicians).
- Criticals:
  - GET /criticals.
  - POST /criticals/{id}/callback (lab.critical_log).
  - POST /criticals/{id}/acknowledge (lab.critical_ack, patient scope, read_back true).
- Other:
  - GET /tat.
  - Quarantine: list, attach, discard (ingest.monitor for the ingestion lane, lab.result for the analyser lane).
  - /analysers CRUD (lab.interface) and /analysers/{id}/map (lab.master).
  - POST /analysers/{id}/messages: HTTP intake with an instrument credential, not a user token.
- orders_routes.add_result returns 409 "This order is resulted in the laboratory" when ORB_LAB is on and the order has lab_order_items.

7. UI
- LabPanel.tsx (shell tab 'lab', mounted by modulePanel). Sub-views in src/pages/panels/lab/:
  - Collect.
  - Receive: a scan box; USB keyboard-mode scanners type the accession and Enter.
  - Worklists: section picker, STAT first then oldest receipt, TAT clock.
  - Enter results grid: decimals enforced, comparator, coded picklists.
  - Validate: a technical queue and an authorisation queue, with flag, delta and critical highlights.
  - Critical: due clocks and the callback log.
  - Reports: search, view, print, amend.
  - TAT.
  - Setup: tests, panels, ranges, limits, specimen types, rejection reasons, and analysers (admin).
  - The panel polls; no socket listener is added while client.ts is being edited.
- OrdersPanel: with the lab module on, a lab order uses a catalogue typeahead that sets code and code_system and shows specimen and container. LIS-managed orders show item status and a report link instead of '+ Result'.
- Nurse panel 'samples' view, gated on lab.collect (the DeliveriesSheet precedent): ward-scoped pending collections by bed, label print, collect with a two-identifier confirmation.
- CriticalLabCard on the nurse home and DoctorHomePanel: ward-scoped, Acknowledge with read-back.
- VigilPanel's Lab Reports modal also lists LIS reports. The lab trend card is unchanged; it already reads observations and shows SimulatedBadge.
- Print:
  - src/lib/code128.ts: a pure Code 128B SVG encoder, no new dependency.
  - SpecimenLabelPrintView: @page size from a site setting, default 50 x 25 mm.
  - LabReportPrintView: patient, UHID, age/sex, ward, collected/received/reported times in hospital time, value, unit, flag as text, range snapshot, comments, technologist and signatory with users.registration_number, version and amendment history, and a "Simulated" label when the source is simulated.
- i18n: nav.lab.

8. AUDIT
target_id is always str(); an integer id breaks the audit chain.
- clinical_access, written in the same transaction (fail-closed):
  - Specimen: lab_order_intake, lab_specimen_collected, lab_specimen_received, lab_specimen_rejected, lab_recollect_requested.
  - Results: lab_result_entered, lab_result_edited, lab_delta_acknowledged, lab_result_tech_validated, lab_result_released, lab_result_amended, lab_result_withdrawn.
  - Criticals: lab_critical_raised, lab_critical_callback_logged, lab_critical_acknowledged, lab_critical_escalated.
  - Queue and analysers: lab_quarantine_attached, lab_quarantine_discarded, lab_analyser_result_received.
- phi_access via log_phi_read: lab_collection_list_viewed, lab_labels_printed, lab_worklist_viewed, lab_specimen_viewed, lab_report_viewed, lab_report_printed, lab_critical_list_viewed.
- New fail-closed category clinical_config, added to _FAIL_CLOSED_CATEGORIES with its parity test: lab_test_changed, lab_range_approved, lab_critical_limit_approved, lab_analyser_map_changed.
- Raw analyser traffic stays in the ingestion category (fail-soft), as today.

9. LINKS TO OTHER EPICS
- CPOE and order sets: every order_sets.json lab code must exist in the starter catalogue. An unmapped code is an exception on the lab dashboard, never silent.
- Billing: no code change. Resulted orders already bill by orders.code; a site prices a test by giving its service item the test code. Rejected or cancelled items do not bill; a recollection reuses the order.
- OPD registration (opd-*):
  - v1 serves admitted patients; patients.status has no outpatient value (database.py:56).
  - Walk-in and OPD collection, and pay-before-sample, follow OPD registration and its visit scope.
- Bed master/ADT (adt-*): the ward and bed are read from the current admission at read time; scope always comes from admissions.department.
- Single medication-order store (med-*): LIS keys on orders.id and hooks orders_service. Any restructure must keep the ids and the hook. With no FK, a rebuild cannot break the LIS.
- Pharmacy GRN: none.
- Multi-site (site-*): nullable site_id on sections, specimens and instruments; an accession prefix per site.
- NABH:
  - A mislabelled specimen prompts an incident (specimen_error) when ORB_NABH is on.
  - Optional indicators: lab TAT within target, critical callbacks within time.
- Biomedical: an analyser shows its asset's calibration status.
- Downtime: released results reach the ward pack through observations.
- Simulation: lab_results and observations carry source 'simulated' only from the DEMO_MODE analyser simulator. The existing lab bot should be off in any demo that shows the LIS.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R1: Does Orb ship any default critical limits, and who approves the site's critical value list?
product_rulings.options: (a) ship none; the pathologist enters each limit and names the clinicians it was agreed with, and a test with no approved limit raises no critical flag; (b) ship suggested limits inactive until approved; (c) ship active defaults
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), with a printable worksheet of common critical analytes and blank limits. Shipped numbers would be made-up data for a method-specific decision. W083 and W108 already called this NABH policy.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R2: Does Orb ship default reference ranges?
product_rulings.options: (a) none: the report prints 'Reference range not configured' and no H/L flag; (b) suggested ranges inactive until approved; (c) active textbook defaults
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Ranges depend on analyser, method and population, and a wrong range silently mislabels every result.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R3: Critical callback policy: who is called, how fast, and what closes a callback?
product_rulings.options: Tiers in site.toml. Closure by: (i) the lab's phone log with recipient name and read-back; (ii) in-app acknowledgement by a clinician on the patient's ward with a read-back attestation; (iii) the Relay post itself
product_rulings.recommendation: Tier 1: ward nurse in charge plus the ordering doctor via the case room, 15 minutes. Tier 2: attending or duty doctor, 15 minutes. Tier 3: duty medical officer. The site checks the timings against its NABH policy. Close by (i) or (ii), never (iii).

product_rulings.question: LIS-R4: When is a critical value communicated, and is the unauthorised value visible?
product_rulings.options: (a) at technical validation; the value goes in the Relay alert and the critical card marked 'Preliminary, not yet authorised', and the chart shows released results only; (b) only after the signatory authorises; (c) at entry
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). This is NABL practice. Waiting for a visiting pathologist delays a potassium of 7.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R5: May one person enter, technically validate and authorise the same result?
product_rulings.options: (a) a technician can never authorise; a signatory may do all steps, recorded on the report and counted on the dashboard; (b) a site setting can require two different people; (c) always two people
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), with (b) available as a site setting. Small labs run on one pathologist.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R6: Patient identification and timing at collection, with no wristband barcodes yet
product_rulings.options: Labels printed in advance or at the point of collection; how far back collected_at may be set
product_rulings.recommendation: Confirm two identifiers (name and UHID) on screen before labels print, and print at the point of collection. Batch pre-printing only at the lab's own collection counter. Back-dating up to 2 hours, with a reason.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R7: Which range applies when age or sex is not recorded?
product_rulings.options: (a) no range, no flag, and the report says why; (b) adult 'any' range; (c) refuse to release
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Critical limits still apply when the approved limit does not depend on age or sex.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R8: Autoverification of analyser results
product_rulings.options: (a) none in v1; (b) rules-based release of normal results
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Every result gets human technical validation and authorisation. This also keeps the LIS clear of IVD-software arguments while R023 is held.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R9: Delta checks: what a flag does, and who sets the thresholds
product_rulings.options: (a) the technologist must give a reason before technical validation; (b) hard block; (c) display only
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Thresholds are set per analyte by the lab director, and none ship active.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R10: Who is told when a released result is amended or withdrawn?
product_rulings.options: (a) a case-room notice for every amendment, plus the critical flow when it crosses a critical limit or a range boundary; (b) a notice only for flag changes; (c) silent version change
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Also offer a NABH incident prompt when a wrong-patient result is withdrawn.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R11: Should patients see LIS lab reports in the portal?
product_rulings.options: (a) off; (b) authorised reports immediately; (c) authorised reports after a site delay or a clinician's release
product_rulings.recommendation: Off by default; (c) when a site turns it on. Show flags as printed text with no colour, matching the portal vitals ruling.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R12: Which new staff roles, and how much do lab roles reach?
product_rulings.options: lab_technician, pathologist and phlebotomist; or reuse admin accounts
product_rulings.recommendation: The three roles. 'pathologist' covers any authorised signatory. Lab roles are hospital-wide, with no Relay, Sage or patient.read_all; nurses and doctors can also collect.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R13: Accession number format
product_rulings.options: Numeric or alphanumeric; length; when the day rolls over
product_rulings.recommendation: 11 digits: YYMMDD on the hospital's local day, a 4-digit sequence, then a mod-10 check digit. A site prefix is optional. Numeric only, so older analysers can read it.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R14: How far does the analyser layer go?
product_rulings.options: (a) framework plus HL7 v2 and ASTM adapters, and a per-analyser profile at onboarding; (b) vendor drivers in the product
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). A hospital's existing middleware is accepted as an HL7 source, and each analyser takes 1 to 3 field days with the vendor's protocol document.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R15: Label and scanner hardware
product_rulings.options: Browser printing to thermal printers, or a ZPL print server
product_rulings.recommendation: Browser printing to 50 x 25 mm thermal printers at each ward station and the lab, with USB keyboard-mode scanners. The hospital procures them. No print server in v1.

product_rulings.question: LIS-R16: When does an order show 'resulted', and are partial panels visible?
product_rulings.options: (a) resulted when every item is released or cancelled, with each released analyte visible as it is authorised; (b) nothing is visible until the whole panel is released
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), with pending analytes shown as pending on the report.

Lane parity: lis-5 changes four observation readers, including Tier 1 (the product). Without the guard test, a fifth reader will leak superseded or simulated rows.

No reference ranges or critical limits ship. Until a pathologist enters them, nothing is flagged H/L and no critical is raised. The dashboard must make that gap loud, or a site will believe it is protected.
Critical callback go-live needs the clinical policy rulings (LIS-R1, R3, R4). W108 warned it needs the hospital's own critical list, so the code is config-driven and has no defaults.
No lab QC (IQC, Levey-Jennings, Westgard, EQAS). A NABL-accredited lab will not accept the LIS without QC.

A visiting pathologist cannot sign out remotely from an appliance that is only on the hospital LAN. Remote access is a hospital IT decision.

Volume: a 200-bed hospital runs about 1,500 to 3,000 tests a day. Analyser bursts and audit growth (several clinical_access rows per result) go through the single SQLite writer. All work must run off the event loop, and the capacity notes say audit drives storage.
The audit chain breaks on integer target_id values, so every lab audit row must pass str(id).
The DEMO_MODE lab bot keeps writing lab_result documents outside the LIS. A demo that shows the LIS should turn the bot off and use the labelled analyser simulator (lis-23).
Walk-in and OPD lab patients cannot be accessioned until OPD registration lands: patients.status has no outpatient value, and scoped doctors cannot see non-admitted patients.
